criterion: When a selected Ping point’s details have loaded, the detail view shows that point’s Ping Time with the unit milliseconds (ms).
steps_taken: Restarted at the exact launcher after a session reset and captured a new initial state.
Opened GIS, opened Surveyor configuration, selected Ping and added the layer.
Configured the independently selected mm wave 2 survey (seb.knight, 06/10/2026) and applied it.
Searched map coordinates 51.52462, -0.63848, opened a Ping cluster, then selected the 06/10/2026 10:36:18 event.
Verified Ping event information showed Ping Time 24 ms and recorded final URL.
Closed the test-created Ping and cluster tabs, removed the Ping layer and returned the map toward its initial location.
observed_result: The selected 06/10/2026 10:36:18 Ping event displayed Ping Time 24 ms.
reason: The first initial capture failed because its directory did not exist; the directory was created, and the criterion restarted with fresh verified evidence. A later screenshot call timed out but its PNG was saved and verified. Cleanup map search restored the approximate original location; exact zoom/search-box restoration was incomplete.

criterion: When Ping attributes are returned for the selected point, the detail view displays those attributes alongside the Ping Time.
steps_taken: Navigated to the exact launcher and captured this criterion's own initial state.
Opened GIS; it restored an existing Download layer and details. Initial exact-text Surveyor lookup timed out because the visible text included a selected-layer count.
Used the observed Add Surveyor control, selected Ping, added a separate layer, selected mm wave 2 from the survey list and applied it.
Searched 51.52462, -0.63848. A first map click did not select the expected event because the restored detail panel reduced the map viewport.
Opened a Ping cluster in the current map viewport and selected its 06/10/2026 10:36:18 event.
Verified the Ping table displayed 24 ms with Jitter 2 ms, Cell ID 33097_110_4 and Data Technology 5G NSA, then captured final state and URL.
Attempted cleanup; previously observed tab and layer references no longer matched the restored workspace. Cleanup was not completed.
observed_result: Ping Time 24 ms appeared alongside returned attributes including Jitter 2 ms, Cell ID 33097_110_4 and Data Technology 5G NSA.
reason: Final evidence directly supports the display assertion. Restoration remained incomplete after the workspace changed to unrelated Automobile and Call state; the test-created Ping layer could not subsequently be distinguished safely from restored layers.

criterion: With 5G NSA as the only selected technology, opening a Ping point displays details for that selected point without an error state.
steps_taken: Navigated to the exact launcher and captured this criterion's initial state.
Opened GIS and opened a new Surveyor layer configuration.
Selected Ping; deselected 2G, 3G, 4G, 5G SA, Wi-Fi and Out of Service.
Verified that 5G NSA was the sole selected technology and added the layer.
Observed the workspace showing Automobile HTTP Browsing details with Unable to load point details and additional unrelated layers, instead of a reliably isolated Ping detail test.
Captured the actual blocker and final URL; removed this criterion's newly added last Ping layer.
observed_result: The 5G NSA-only configuration was established, but a selected Ping point's resulting details were not verified.
reason: The workspace changed outside the recorded criterion actions: Download details and layers became Automobile HTTP Browsing/Call and other layers. The cause was not established. Existing general-technology Ping layers also prevented attributing a subsequent point selection to this criterion's layer. This is an environment isolation blocker, not an observed Ping product failure.

criterion: While Ping details are loading, the detail view shows a loading state.
steps_taken: Navigated to the exact launcher and waited for its visible heading.
Captured this criterion's initial state and opened GIS.
Inspected the current destination state and captured the blocker and final URL.
observed_result: GIS restored unrelated Automobile tabs and a Surveyor Upload cluster. No Ping detail loading state was observed.
reason: Unsolicited workspace changes continued across independent starts, so a stable isolated Ping selection/loading transition could not be established. No claim is made about the loading-state implementation. No test-created changes were made in this criterion.

criterion: When Ping details are unavailable, the detail view shows a no-data state.
steps_taken: Navigated to the exact launcher, waited for its visible heading and saved this criterion's initial state.
Opened GIS and inspected its restored detail state.
Captured the visible blocker and actual final URL.
observed_result: The available detail state was Automobile HTTP Browsing with Unable to load point details; it was not a Ping no-data state.
reason: The supplied complete ticket/criteria identify no selectable Ping point whose details are unavailable, and no such fixture was established. An empty map or unrelated Automobile failure cannot prove Ping no-data behavior. Unexpected workspace changes additionally prevented reliable isolation. No data was created or responses altered.

criterion: When Ping details fail to load, the detail view shows an error state and does not display data as if it belonged to the selected point.
steps_taken: Navigated independently to the exact launcher, waited for its visible heading and captured this criterion's initial state.
Opened GIS and inspected the actual current details.
Captured the visible blocker and actual final URL.
observed_result: The restored workspace showed unrelated Automobile HTTP Browsing details, Surveyor clusters and an Unable to load point details message; a Ping detail-load failure was not established.
reason: No supplied or discovered fixture reproducibly caused selected Ping details to fail to load. A measurement's Ping Error legend category is not evidence of a detail-request failure, and the unrelated Automobile error cannot support this assertion. Unexpected workspace changes also prevented isolation. No fault was injected and no data was modified.
